title: US-Iran Draft Peace Deal 'Within 24 Hours'; Trump: Deal 'Largely Negotiated'; Vance, Witkoff, Kushner, Qalifbaf Approve Draft; 60-Day Bridge Ceasefire; Hormuz Reopening on Table
detail: On May 23, 2026, the Washington Times reported exclusively that the United States and Iran were expected to announce a draft peace agreement within 24 hours — the most significant diplomatic breakthrough since the April ceasefire. The Washington Times reported that senior negotiators — Vice President JD Vance, Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner, and Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalifbaf — had approved the draft proposal. President Trump confirmed publicly that the deal was 'largely negotiated' and separately stated that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen under the framework. The mechanism under negotiation is a 60-day ceasefire extension serving as a bridge to formal nuclear talks — structured to decouple the immediate military standoff (de facto ceasefire, Hormuz blockade, ~750 vessels trapped) from the complex long-term nuclear framework. Key unresolved issues as of May 23 include: the disposition of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile (~400–460 kg at 60% purity, upgradeable to weapons-grade in 1–2 weeks); sanctions relief sequencing (Iran demands sanctions lifted before enrichment curtailment; US demands curtailment before relief); and Strait of Hormuz transit fees. Pakistan's Army Chief General Asim Munir is playing a key intermediary role, continuing Pakistan's function as the principal US–Iran diplomatic conduit since the collapse of direct Islamabad rounds in April. NPR confirmed Trump's statement that the deal is 'largely negotiated' and that Hormuz reopening is part of the package. Bloomberg reported Iran-US signals of progress. The Washington Post confirmed the US is seeking a ceasefire extension while maintaining war threats as leverage. Arab News, citing Gulf diplomatic sources, reported both parties saying they could be close to agreement. The Hormuz blockade entering its 12th week has created the greatest global shipping disruption since the Suez Crisis. Iran's inflation is running at approximately 53.7%. A 60-day ceasefire bridge — if agreed — would be the most consequential peace milestone in the US–Iran conflict since the April 10 ceasefire declaration.

title: Colombia Election 8 Days Out: Cepeda at 44.3%; Right-Wing Split May Hand Cepeda First Round but Runoff Outcome Uncertain — Peace Architecture at Stake
detail: Eight days before Colombia's presidential election on May 31, 2026, new polling data published on May 23 deepened the uncertainty about the outcome and its implications for Colombia's peace architecture. A Noticias Caracol/Blu Radio poll placed left-wing Senator Iván Cepeda (Pacto Histórico) at 44.3% in the first round, right-wing Abelardo De la Espriella at 21.5%, and center-right Paloma Valencia at 19.8%. However, a separate poll from the May 18–21 period showed that in a direct Cepeda-Valencia runoff scenario, Valencia leads 44.6% to 41.5% — within margin of error, but suggesting that the right-wing vote could consolidate against Cepeda in a runoff. The AS/COA poll tracker placed Cepeda at 44% and De la Espriella at 27%, with the right-wing split between De la Espriella and Valencia as the critical variable determining whether the first round produces a majority. The City Paper Bogotá reported that Valencia 'doubles in race' — her numbers have grown from single digits to 20%+, making a three-candidate race increasingly competitive but not foreclosing Cepeda's path. The peace-process implications remain the election's defining stakes: a Cepeda presidency would resume ELN peace negotiations suspended since the January 2025 Catatumbo massacre and potentially re-engage FARC-EMC dissidents; a Valencia presidency would pursue a military-first approach while maintaining JEP processes; a De la Espriella presidency would immediately terminate all peace negotiations. The ELN's unilateral pre-election ceasefire declared February 2026 is nominally holding in most areas. US Senator Moreno's May 21 warning about potential non-recognition of results has heightened political tensions going into the final week.

title: Zelensky: Ukraine Waiting for US Signal on Next Peace Round as Iran Deal Negotiations Absorb Washington's Diplomatic Bandwidth
detail: On May 23, 2026, President Zelensky stated publicly that Ukraine is waiting for a US signal on the next round of peace talks with Russia, noting that Washington has not reestablished a structured negotiating format since the Istanbul talks collapsed on May 16 in under two hours. Ukrainian officials observed that Washington's diplomatic bandwidth is now substantially consumed by the Iran nuclear deal negotiations — where a draft agreement was reported as imminent on May 23 (Trump: 'largely negotiated') — leaving the Ukraine-Russia mediation track in a holding pattern. Zelensky reiterated efforts to bring European leaders more directly into negotiations, citing European Council President António Costa as a potential alternative facilitation channel. Russian Foreign Ministry signals from May 19 of openness to the Istanbul format have not produced a concrete offer of new talks. The structural gaps remain unbridged: Russia demands recognition of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson as Russian territory; Ukraine refuses territorial concessions without NATO-equivalent security guarantees. The full-scale war continues on a 1,000-km front with no ceasefire in force since the US-brokered 72-hour pause expired May 11. Pravda EU reported that Zelensky was specifically waiting for a US signal 'by end of the week.' The concentration of US diplomatic energy on the Iran deal on May 23–24 makes a Ukraine breakthrough this week highly unlikely, per multiple Western analysts. The first POW exchange tranche of 205-for-205 was completed May 15 — the sole tangible diplomatic output of the Istanbul round.
